fixed.explanation: In innerAsLocators for internal:role, name and description each set options.exact from attr.caseSensitive and throw on mismatch. A regex value parses as case sensitive, so next to a non-exact string it counts as a conflict and the output falls back to the raw selector. The fix applies the exactness check and assignment only to string values. Regex values are ignored.

query.intent: The selector-to-locator-call conversion (asLocator / locator generator) for role selectors bails out when name and description have conflicting exact flags. A regular expression is parsed as case sensitive (exact), so next to a non-exact string it counts as a conflict. The check should ignore regex values when comparing exactness of name and description.
query.symptom: A getByRole locator with a regex name and string description (or the reverse) prints as the raw internal role selector with [name=...][description=...] instead of the readable getByRole call.

history.analysis: The shown code is the engine and selector builder, not the selector-to-locator converter. The exact-conflict check is likely in the locator generator that converts internal:role selectors to getByRole calls.
